text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: prod-streaming-gateway — spike in 5xx (502/504) and TCP resets detected from upstream pools. 5m error rate 8.4% (baseline ~0.3%). Affected region: us-west1. Alerting SRE and oncall. grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/streaming

Maya (oncall): ACK. I'm oncall for this shift. grabbing logs now. tagging @Sam for runtime help.

Sam (sre): on it. quick q: is this only chunked endpoints or all streaming routes?

Ingrid (support): customer reports incoming — 3 high-tier customers seeing intermittent disconnects during long-stream responses. reported "partial output then connection closed".

Maya (oncall): initial check: 502 spikes correlate w/ upstream resets to runtime pool group A (gpu-pool-a). Also seeing client cancellations climb.

Leo (runtime): I see increased retransmits on the TCP layer + upstream process restarts for a handful of containers. Might be OOM or keepalive dropout. Pulling container logs.

Sam (sre): can someone run a quick curl repro against a known streaming route? want to capture headers and chunk boundaries.

Maya (oncall): running curl now:
```
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.prod/stream/v1/chat/stream?model=rlhf-x >> out.log
```
Result: connection open, first chunk arrives, then after ~12s connection reset by peer. log shows: "upstream prematurely closed connection" and repeated "client canceled" from gateway.

Leo (runtime): paste from runtime logs:
```
[2026-10-05T14:12:01Z] ERROR upstream: read ECONNRESET from client 10.4.5.23:45712
[2026-10-05T14:12:02Z] WARN kv-cache: cache miss, seq len 128
[2026-10-05T14:12:13Z] ERROR process: segfault after oom? pid=2345, rss 7.9GB
```
Noting one process killed by OOM killer, but only a few.

Sam (sre): interesting. two pathways: (A) runtime worker crash causing upstream to close and gateway surfaces 502, (B) gateway backpressure/timeouts closing streams mid-flight. Which looks more prevalent?

Maya (oncall): metrics: 60% of 5xx correlate to container restarts (ooms) in pool A. 40% show gateway timeouts with no container restart. So mixed.

Ingrid (support): escalation from customer Alpha: "we lost partial transcripts for 8 of 30 live sessions in the last hour" — they're asking for mitigation asap.

Sam (sre): immediate live mitigations:
- move traffic off pool A to pool B (less loaded) via routing tag (canary shift 30% → 100% if stable).
- enable gateway graceful fallback: switch streaming->polling for affected customers as temporary mitigation.
- increase gateway upstream timeout to 90s from 30s for streaming routes to avoid premature closes.

Maya (oncall): starting traffic migration now. running:
```
rbctl route update streaming --tag remove=poolA add=poolB --percent=30
```
I'll watch error rates.

deploy-bot: Note: routing change created rollout id r-20261005-1872.

Maya (oncall): 10 minutes after shift: error rate dropped from 8.4% -> 1.1%. container restarts on poolA continue but reduced impact since less traffic.

Leo (runtime): parallel: I'm deploying a hotfix to avoid OOM in rare codepath — reduces peak memory use by ~200MB. patch queued to canary 5% now.

Sam (sre): gateway timeout change applied to streaming virtualhost (nginx/proxy): set proxy_read_timeout 90s and proxy_buffering off for /stream.

Maya (oncall): client cancellation metric still elevated for long-lived sessions — looks like some clients explicitly reset after partial frames (maybe client-side timeout). Need to communicate fallback options to partnerships and docs.

Ingrid (support): drafting message to affected customers: short explanation + recommended retry logic (use resume tokens, idempotent reconnection, backoff). Will share in #customer-impact for approval.

Sam (sre): on-pager followup items:
- confirm hotfix results on canary, then promote to 25%/50%/100% if stable.
- investigate memory spike root cause (heap/profile) and add guardrails (cgroup mem limit tuning + early refuse on high mem).
- add streaming-level circuit breaker to prevent a single noisy client from exhausting worker memory.
- add metric for "partial-frame since last keepalive" to detect this pattern earlier.

Maya (oncall): recording incident classification: P1 for customer impact (partial transcript loss for paid customers). Notifying oncall rotation for SRE to follow through.

Leo (runtime): quick datapoint from canary: hotfix cut memory spikes by 30% and no segfaults after 20m. Increasing canary to 25%.

deploy-bot: Rollout r-20261005-1872 updated: routing 60% -> poolB; canary hotfix h-20261005-5 at 25%.

Maya (oncall): error rate now stable ~0.6% for streaming. customer reports from Alpha say reconnect success and fewer partials. I'll keep monitoring for next 2 hours.

Ingrid (support): message ready for customers, includes suggested client-side fixes (increase client read timeout, enable reconnect with resume token, exponential backoff).

Sam (sre): post-incident actions (short):
1) run memprof across models used in poolA and track allocations.
2) add autoscale to poolA to avoid headroom collapse.
3) add graceful drains when route shifts happen to avoid connection drops.
4) update runbooks: streaming partial-frame troubleshooting checklist.

Maya (oncall): leaving detailed notes in incident ticket #INC-20261005-73. handing off to Sam for follow-up. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Sam (sre): taking handoff. will file follow-ups and schedule a blameless postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident marked as acknowledged -> mitigated by user action. Metrics show sustained improvement.

Maya (oncall): ending oncall handoff — last check at 1872502099 UTC.
